responses.prompt: Who prepared the first draft of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
responses.response_text:
The first draft of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was prepared by John Humphrey, a Canadian lawyer and diplomat, who was the Director of the Human Rights Division of the United Nations Secretariat at the time. Humphrey was tasked by the UN Secretary-General, Trygve Halvdan Lie, to prepare a preliminary draft of the Declaration.

Humphrey's draft, which was completed in June 1947, was based on various sources, including the United States Bill of Rights, the French Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen, and the draft of the International Bill of Rights prepared by the Institute of International Law.

Humphrey's draft was then reviewed and revised by a committee of experts, known as the "Drafting Committee", which consisted of representatives from eight countries: Australia, China, France, Lebanon, the Soviet Union, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Yugoslavia. The committee was chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt, the wife of former US President Franklin D. Roosevelt, who played a key role in the drafting and adoption of the UDHR.

The Drafting Committee made significant changes to Humphrey's draft, and the revised text was then submitted to the UN Commission on Human Rights, which made further revisions. The final text of the UDHR was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on December 10, 1948.
